pairs.difference: A: navy cap with an orange band and tassel on cyan rings. It is a cool hero with one warm accent, and the shadows stay a rich blue-violet. B: the hat crown and brim are almost colourless charcoal (subject chroma 0.059, below the real range). In the lens the crown shadows turn into the same purple as the magenta-violet backdrop, so the hat loses its own colour (shadow kept 0.53). Only the yellow band carries colour.
pairs.fix: Give the witch hat a clear local colour, such as a deep plum-violet felt that stays saturated in its shadows. Keep the backdrop a contrasting cool or warm hue instead of the same purple.

pairs.difference: A: a white and blue plane on a blue sky. It repeats the backdrop hue, but the whites stay clean and neutral, as on the real computer card. B: the bat's body and wings are grey-purple at low chroma (0.073), and in the lens the whole bat merges into the violet-pink sky. Hero and backdrop share one hue family, and the only accent is the small yellow eyes.
pairs.fix: Paint the bat in a warmer dark brown-grey with pink ear and wing membranes that read separately. Set it against a contrasting backdrop, such as a teal or deep blue night sky, rather than a violet sky the same hue as its shadows.

pairs.difference: A: saturated red gloves on a blue plank wall and an orange wood floor. It has three clear hue roles, and the shadows stay deep red. B: an acid lime lawn, magenta-to-violet stripes and an orange-brown trunk, all at similar loudness, with no neutral area to rest the eye (5.1 hue families). In the lens the trunk's shadow side flips to backdrop purple.
pairs.fix: Tone the lawn down to a softer, less acid green or cut it back. Keep the trunk's shadows a darker warm brown instead of purple, and let the purple stripes be the one cool field behind a warm brown tree.

pairs.difference: A: a green topiary on green hedges and a green lawn, with almost no warm colour (warm share 0.046). The hero repeats the hue of most of the backdrop, and only the sky separates it. B: a green slide on hot pink waves with cyan rails. The hero and backdrop sit on opposite hues, as on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Put the green topiary in front of a contrasting backdrop, such as a warm peach or pink patterned wall or sunset sky. Add warm terracotta to the planter ring so the green hero is not surrounded by green.

pairs.difference: A: a gold mirror on a green gradient, a warm hero on a cool field. B: a blue machine on a violet gradient, a cool hero on an adjacent cool hue with almost no warm colour (warm share 0.026). Its shadows go blue-violet into the floor, and only the small cans add warm notes.
pairs.fix: Set the blue vending machine on a warm backdrop, such as a yellow or orange sunburst, so the cool hero sits against an opposite temperature.

pairs.difference: A: pink, orange and green signs plus warm-lit balconies against a navy night. The warm hero clearly opposes the cool backdrop. B: the house walls and roof are nearly colourless grey (subject chroma 0.057). In the lens the walls read as a dull khaki, and the only colour on the hero comes from the yellow window glow.
pairs.fix: Give the house its own colours: warm tan or cream stone walls, a slate-blue roof and a red-brown door, kept saturated in shadow so the hero reads warm against the navy night.

pairs.difference: A: red brick pillars, a copper-brown gate, a peach path and a blue sky. The local colours are believable and the shadows stay brick-red. B: a black iron gate and pale grey stone pillars on a navy night, with a mauve-grey cobble path. The hero is almost neutral (chroma 0.038, the lowest in this set), and its shadows go grey (kept 0.56). The small gold padlock is the only colour on the hero.
pairs.fix: Paint the gate in a coloured metal, such as dark green or bronze iron, and make the pillars warm sandstone with saturated brown-orange shadows, so the hero carries colour against the blue night.

pairs.difference: A: blue shoes on an orange and cream setting, a cool hero on a warm field like the real camera card. The confetti accents are busy but the shadows stay blue. B: an orange pumpkin on a purple vignette gradient. The background is very loud (0.216, at the top of the real range), and in the lens the floor shadow and the pumpkin's dark side both pick up pink-violet, so the shadows lean into the backdrop hue.
pairs.fix: Lower the purple backdrop to a calmer mid violet, keep the pumpkin's shadow side a deep burnt orange-brown, and make the cast shadow a darker plum rather than hot pink.

pairs.difference: A: a beige stone fountain with cyan water on yellow stripes. The cool accent and the neutral stone rest the eye. B: candlelight floods the dark brown table in an orange pool, and the silver candelabra picks up peach and orange on its lit side and purple in its shadows. The hero's metal loses its own neutral grey, and the lower half of the card is a single orange-brown mass.
pairs.fix: Keep the candelabra a clean cool silver-grey with blue-grey shadows, and replace the orange glow on the table with a lighter, calmer wood, so the warm candle flames are the only orange accent.

pairs.difference: A: a lime palm and a tan trunk on a magenta swirl over sand, a green hero against the complementary pink. B: a teal orb on a gold stand, but the lower half of the card is a dark, desaturated brown wood table. In the lens the gold stand turns pink-brown and merges with the table, so the gold loses its yellow local colour.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark wood table, or make it a lighter warm tone, and keep the gold stand a bright yellow-gold with orange shadows, so the teal orb and the gold read against the magenta swirl.

pairs.difference: A: the broom's handle, bristles and red tie collapse into one red-brown mass in the lens. The bristles are a saturated orange-gold and the handle a strong red-brown, with no lighter straw or neutral tones. B: red, orange, teal and purple balloons on a sky. That is many hues, but each balloon keeps a believable local colour and pink-red shadows.
pairs.fix: Paint the bristles as pale straw yellow with light tan highlights and the handle as a medium natural wood, so the broom has two clearly different local colours instead of one orange-brown mass.

pairs.difference: A: an orange-rimmed clock on green stripes. It matches the real anchor card, with a warm rim on a cool field and red-brown rim shadows. B: a white marble lion on green lawn and trees. The hero is nearly colourless (chroma 0.027), and its shadows go grey-green from the grass, so the hero repeats the backdrop hue and has no colour of its own.
pairs.fix: Give the lion statue a warm local colour, such as honey sandstone or a golden-bronze patina with orange-brown shadows, so it stands as a warm hero against the green garden.

pattern: Generated cards often have a nearly colourless hero (black, grey or white stone) whose shadows take the backdrop hue (purple, navy or green) instead of a darker version of its own colour. They also use soft vignette gradients or dark brown tables where the real cards have bright rays, stripes or rings. Warm glow pools (candles, windows) turn neutral metal and wood orange-brown. Real cards keep a clear local colour on the hero, warm against a cool field, with rich related shadows.
